doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

chapter: Own records and the music business
title: Where his compositions come from
summary: He explains writing 'Sixth Sense', 'Message From Art' and 'Kind of Bill'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So as a composer I see a piano behind you. Where do your compositional ideas start?

They come from anywhere, you know. I don’t know how familiar you are with any of my records but “Native Land” for example, on that one I’ve got I think five originals, and this tune called “Sixth Sense” which is actually in 5/4 but the melody is a subdivision of 7 over 5. So that came to mind when I was practicing something at the drumset — I’m playing two with my bass drums, three with my hi-hat, and seven or five on the snare

drum. And I’m hearing all of this stuff just layering very nicely, and I thought you know there’s a possibility for a tune in here. So I started to hear something. Then on my first record, “Message From Art” which is a dedication to Art Blakey, that came to me like bam as I was driving on the freeway. And I mean it came in fully composed and by the time I got home I was able to write it out. Yeah. Don’t even ask — I don’t know how. It’s just the way it is you know.
I can picture that, like don’t talk to me for a minute, I’ve got to get this down or I’m going to lose it.
Yeah, exactly. The tune “Kind of Bill” that’s on that same album I worked on that for almost ten years. I mean it was a struggle, a struggle. But I finally got that thing.
Working at it sitting at the piano?
Yes. Oh absolutely, that was a total piano tune, had to be, Bill Evans.
